To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the term supervised learning is not a brand name and (ii) learning is not possible without supervision.

(1) the success of supervised learning in deep learning is due to its ability to capture the statistical structure of the data and not to a specific type of learning or to a lack of inductive biases; (2) supervised learning can also be applied to biological data and it can help us understand how learning works in nature; and (3) supervised learning is not an obstacle for out-of-distribution learning but a prerequisite for it.

(1) supervised learning, in the broadest sense, is the only kind of learning that is possible, and (2) the key to generalization is to use the correct inductive bias, and this can be achieved by choosing the right supervised learning task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
supervised learning and we should be proud to say so.
supervised learning and we should not be shy of admitting it.

the following questions: What are the theoretical and empirical insights about learning and generalisation that can be extracted from biological learning? What is the role of supervision in learning and generalization? How do the insights from biological learning inform artificial neural networks? What is the relationship between supervised learning, inductive biases and generalization? What is the impact of the name of the learning paradigm?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supervised learning is the most powerful learning paradigm and that we should use it more often, not less.
supervised learning is not the problem.
supervised learning is the only way to go.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the renaissance of neural networks is the consequence of a renaissance of supervised learning.
the renaissance of artificial intelligence was catalysed and sustained by supervised learning.
the renaissance of artificial intelligence is not a matter of supervised learning, but rather of learning in general.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the success of classification tasks is not an argument for the superiority of the models, nor a reason to dismiss supervised learning.
supervised learning is not an obstacle to be avoided, but a powerful tool that should be used in conjunction with unsupervised learning to achieve generalization.
the community should focus on the development and understanding of supervised learning models, rather than on the development of new brand names.
